riskRegister.use: Expo CLI and Expo code-signing tooling; not an application runtime dependency.
riskRegister.reachability: The affected RSA signature-verification code was present in Expo tooling. The guarded CI export rejects signing inputs and the package is absent from fresh Web, Android and iOS source maps.
riskRegister.attackerControlledInput: No client or remote-user input is passed to this tooling path during the unsigned export. Signing is outside the gate scope.
riskRegister.rationale: A compatible fixed release is available. node-forge 1.4.2 satisfies the Expo tooling range ^1.3.3 and npm audit no longer reports this advisory.
reviewTriggers: The advisory again matches the installed tree
The dependency moves to an unreviewed root
The package appears in a client bundle

riskRegister.use: Expo CLI and its local development tooling; the application bundles do not import this package.
riskRegister.reachability: The affected validation code is used by Expo tooling. Expo CLI 57 requires Zod 3, while the fixed 4.6.6 release is outside that consumer range. The unsigned export does not start network DevTools.
riskRegister.attackerControlledInput: Application users cannot submit data to this build-time package. Repository configuration can influence local tooling, so acceptance is limited to the credential-free, read-only CI export path.
riskRegister.rationale: The compatible Expo 57 dependency range has no patched Zod 3 release. For the accepted export path, fresh platform source maps, disabled DevTools/signing flows, read-only CI and absent credentials constrain exposure. This does not describe npm audit as clean.
reviewTriggers: A fixed Zod version satisfies every installed consumer range
The advisory range or severity changes
A vulnerable node gains a new root dependency
The package appears in a client bundle

riskRegister.use: Expo configuration tooling and a Workbox build dependency; not imported by the application runtime.
riskRegister.reachability: The library can poison the prototype of a returned merged object when an attacker controls a JSON source object and the target contains a null placeholder. Expo's vulnerable merge helper is used by config-mutation operations, not the allowlisted export command; the Workbox resolver calls deepmerge({}, defaults) only with its own constant defaults, without attacker-controlled JSON or a null-placeholder target. Fresh Web, Android and iOS source maps must continue to omit it.
riskRegister.attackerControlledInput: Static repository configuration is controlled by contributors, but application users have no runtime path to this package. CI runs only the guarded export and Service Worker build with read-only permissions, pinned actions, no secrets, no persisted checkout credentials and no signing inputs.
riskRegister.rationale: The upstream advisory is treated as real despite its Low severity. The vulnerable API shape was reproduced. In the reviewed acceptance flow, the affected merge operation is not invoked, the package is build-only, untrusted inputs have no privileged CI capability, and the package is absent from all client bundles. This residual-risk decision is confined to that flow.
reviewTriggers: The export or Workbox call path begins invoking vulnerable merge behavior
A vulnerable node gains a new root dependency
The package appears in a client bundle
CI gains credentials or write permissions
